summary: We add A, subtract A+1, add A+2, … up to B. A `sign` variable that flips every step keeps track of plus or minus (T1 — simple loop).

blocks.title: Read the range
blocks.text: A and B are on two separate lines, so two `input()` calls.

blocks.title: Set up total and sign
blocks.text: `sign = 1` means the first number is added. The sign depends on the number's **position** in the range, not on whether it is odd — that is why we don't use `x % 2` (it breaks when A is even).

blocks.title: Add with the current sign, then flip
blocks.text: `range(A, B + 1)` includes B. `sign * x` adds or subtracts x, and `sign = -sign` switches between +1 and -1 for the next number.

complexity: Time O(B − A) with up to 10⁶ numbers → about 0.1 s in Python.
pitfalls: Using `x % 2` for the sign — wrong when A is even.
